entities.name: Inkatha Freedom Party
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) is a South African political party founded in 1975 by Mangosuthu Buthelezi as a Zulu cultural and political organization within the KwaZulu homeland, which became a major force in anti-apartheid politics — but one that allied with the apartheid government against the ANC, producing the notorious 'black on black' violence of the 1980s-1990s that killed 14,000 people. The IFP's conflict with the ANC — fueled partly by apartheid security services ('Third Force' operations) — cast a shadow over South Africa's democratic transition.

Buthelezi revived the historical Inkatha movement — founded by Zulu king Solomon ka Dinuzulu in 1922 as a cultural organization — as a political party that embraced Zulu ethnic identity and rejected the ANC's non-ethnic African nationalism. The IFP operated within the apartheid bantustans (homelands), leading to ANC accusations of collaboration. The 1990s Natal-Midlands violence between IFP and ANC supporters — with documented involvement of apartheid security forces arming IFP — was the most brutal political violence in South African history outside apartheid itself.

The Truth and Reconciliation Commission documented apartheid state support for IFP violence. The IFP's participation in the 1994 elections (joining at the last minute after international mediation) was credited with preventing civil war. Buthelezi served as Minister of Home Affairs under Mandela and Mbeki. The IFP remains a significant KwaZulu-Natal political force with approximately 3-4% national vote.
